goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to identify the state, rate and initial condition of a first-order model; translate the rate law into a scaffolded Forward Euler update; trace the loop; compare timesteps at the same final time; and validate the trajectory against physical checks and a supplied exact reference.

deck_context.deck_context: Week 08 introduces first-order ODE simulation through Newton cooling. The visible reasoning chain is physical prediction, state/rate/initial condition, units, Euler discretisation, two hand-traced updates, pseudocode, arrays and indexing, a short MATLAB loop, physical checks, timestep refinement, exact-reference error, defect diagnosis, parameter change, model limitation, and exit ticket.
deck_context.core_claim: An ODE trajectory is built from an initial condition and repeated rate-based updates. A plausible curve is not enough: timestep refinement, a supplied reference, units, bounds, and physical interpretation are needed before trusting it.
deck_context.locked_model: Uniform object temperature T obeys dT/dt = -(T - T_room)/tau, with T_room = 20 degrees Celsius, T(0) = 80 degrees Celsius, tau = 100 s, and 0 <= t <= 300 s. Forward Euler timesteps are 50, 25, and 12.5 s. Temperature differences in degrees Celsius have the same numerical size as differences in kelvin.
deck_context.locked_evidence: With h = 50 s: T0 = 80 C at 0 s, rate0 = -0.60 C/s, T1 = 50 C at 50 s, rate1 = -0.30 C/s, T2 = 35 C at 100 s. Exact T(t) = 20 + 60 exp(-t/100), so exact T(300 s) = 22.9872241021 C. Euler endpoints for h = 50, 25, 12.5 s are 20.9375000000, 21.9005811214, 22.4341342258 C. Absolute errors are 2.0497241021, 1.0866429806, 0.5530898762 C. Doubling tau to 200 s gives exact T(300 s) = 33.3878 C. For h = 25 s, the first Euler value is 65 C.
deck_context.exactness: All equations, signs, code tokens, variable names, time coordinates, array counts, temperatures, rates, units, reference values, error values, graph axes, marker positions, and curve relationships are strict teaching content. Do not invent, omit, or approximate them. Use absolute Celsius temperature error; do not show percentage error based on Celsius temperature.

slides.title: Can a Cooling Rate Predict a Temperature?
slides.intent: Open with a familiar cooling prediction and establish that the goal is a future temperature trajectory.
key_points: A warm object starts at 80 C in a room at 20 C.
Will it lose the same temperature in every equal time interval?
Use a rate law to predict temperature from 0 to 300 s.
slides.local_context: Show a labelled warm object and a cooler constant environment with heat-flow direction. The conceptual visual must agree with cooling toward 20 C; do not show a numerical trajectory yet.

constraints: Use the horizontal divider below the title.
Keep heat flow from the warmer object toward the surroundings.
No slide number, outer frame, logo, watermark, or footer.

slides.title: Name the State, Rate, and Initial Condition
slides.intent: Map each ODE ingredient to its physical meaning and unit before introducing the update.
key_points: State: T(t), object temperature in degrees Celsius.
Rate: dT/dt, temperature change in degrees Celsius per second.
Initial condition: T(0) = 80 C.
Environment: T_room = 20 C; cooling time tau = 100 s.
slides.local_context: Assumptions: the object's temperature is uniform, room temperature is constant, and tau is constant. Use labels next to their physical targets.

layout.composition: central physical object with four labelled callouts arranged around it

constraints: Use exactly T(t), dT/dt, T(0)=80 C, T_room=20 C, tau=100 s.
No slide number or outer frame.

slides.title: Read the Cooling Law in Words
slides.intent: Explain the sign, temperature excess, timescale, and units in the ODE.
key_points: A larger temperature excess gives faster cooling.
The minus sign means temperature decreases while T > 20 C.
At T = 80 C, the rate is -0.60 C/s.
slides.local_context: State the equation in words: cooling rate equals minus temperature excess divided by cooling time. Show degrees Celsius divided by seconds for the rate unit.

layout.composition: large equation on the left with short annotated parts, physical meaning and initial-rate substitution on the right

visual_elements.main_visual: equation split into minus sign, temperature excess, and cooling time

constraints: Preserve the negative sign and -0.60 C/s exactly.
No slide number or outer frame.

slides.title: Turn the Current Rate into One Step
slides.intent: Connect the continuous rate law to one Forward Euler next-value rule and its units.
key_points: Next temperature = current temperature + timestep x current rate.
Seconds x C/s gives a temperature change.
A smaller h recalculates the changing rate sooner.
slides.local_context: Use a current-state arrow to a next-state card. Make current T_n and next T_(n+1) visually distinct without implying the method is exact.

visual_elements.main_visual: T_n -> compute current rate -> add h times rate -> T_(n+1)

constraints: Use the title divider.

slides.title: Read the Euler Loop
slides.intent: Trace which array elements the loop reads and writes, with complete code visible.
key_points: for n = 1:numel(t_s)-1
rate_Cps = -(T_C(n)-T_room_C)/tau_s;
T_C(n+1) = T_C(n) + dt_s*rate_Cps;
When n = 2, read T_C(2) and write T_C(3).
slides.local_context: Render a complete monospaced three-line loop including end. Annotate current index n and next index n+1. Explain that stopping one short keeps the write inside the array.

constraints: Preserve every code token, capitalization, operator, semicolon, and end.

slides.title: Spot a Runnable but Wrong Update
slides.intent: Diagnose the missing timestep factor using units and repair the Euler expression.
key_points: Wrong: T_C(n+1) = T_C(n) + rate_Cps;
Temperature plus temperature/time is dimensionally inconsistent.
Correct: T_C(n+1) = T_C(n) + dt_s*rate_Cps;
A smooth-looking graph is not a validation check.
slides.local_context: Use muted coral for the wrong line and sage for the corrected line. Show C + C/s as the failing unit check and C + s(C/s) = C as the repair.

layout.composition: wrong code and unit failure on the left, corrected code and unit check on the right, diagnostic question below

constraints: Preserve code exactly.
Coral only marks the defect; green marks the repaired line.
No slide number or outer frame.

slides.title: Predict a Slower Cooling Model
slides.intent: Separate a physical parameter change from numerical refinement and state one model limitation.
key_points: Change tau from 100 s to 200 s; keep T(0) = 80 C and T_room = 20 C.
Initial cooling-rate magnitude halves from 0.60 to 0.30 C/s.
Exact T(300 s) changes from 22.9872 C to 33.3878 C.
A smaller timestep cannot fix a nonuniform-temperature or changing-room model limitation.
slides.local_context: Use side-by-side fast and slow cooling conceptual trajectories with exact endpoints labelled. Make clear tau is physical and h is numerical. Do not introduce formal stability analysis.
